correctness.rationale: For all n>=3, every deleted matching leaves G_{n,t} connected. Gravner–Lyu–Sivakoff (arXiv:1610.07320v1, Theorem 3, inspected in full relevant statement) equates synchronization to zero circulation. The two discrete 1-forms differ by an exact factor 3 on closed walks. A unique normalized integer 1-Lipschitz lift encodes each zero-circulation coloring. The A-shore spread is at most two; the s=0,1,2 contributions are respectively 3^n, 4^n-2^(n+1)+t*2^n, and 3^n-2^(n+1)+1+t*2^n+t(t-1). Multiplying their sum by three proves the single exact claim, including all boundaries. Two independently written and replayed finite checkers confirmed all enumerated parameters; finite checks are supporting evidence, not a substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: The probability that a random initial three-color assignment reaches synchronization is a canonical basin-size observable for excitable graph dynamics. The exact matching-deletion response over a two-parameter infinite family isolates non-additive edge-defect interactions: each additional disjoint deletion changes the successful initial-population count by a larger amount, with universal second difference six. The asymptotic rate simultaneously shows the perturbation leaves the leading exponential decay unchanged. Neither a single-graph calculation nor a trivial renaming; structural three-case lift enumeration identifies precisely why the t(t-1) contribution arises.
